editorial.headline: Seaweed Food Processing Meets Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10798 covers food products made from seaweed, nationally open to foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10798 is a manufacturing activity for food ingredients and prepared food products made from seaweed. The record’s Indonesian scope is precise: it covers the making of seaweed-based food preparations such as agar-agar, carrageenan, and nori sheets, as well as other forms of processing seaweed into food preparations. In plain English, this is not seaweed farming, trading, restaurant service, or general packaged-food retail. It is the industrial conversion of seaweed into recognizable food materials and processed edible products.

The scale profile is broad. The slim record opens this activity to Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it is not confined to only one business size. A founder reading the code should see it as a production category that can sit across small, medium, or large operations, depending on the actual business structure and registration path. The common thread is the activity itself: processing seaweed into food products such as agar, carrageenan, and sheet nori. The code is therefore useful for businesses whose core registered activity is the making of these seaweed-derived foods, rather than merely handling seaweed as a raw commodity or selling finished goods made elsewhere.

Nationally, the investment signal is clear. Drawing on Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the record classifies the activity as TERBUKA and sets pma_max_asing at 100. That means the national layer treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. On the national reading alone, a foreign-owned company would not be facing a foreign-shareholding cap inside this record. That national openness matters, but it is not the whole answer for a founder planning to register the activity in Bali.

The Bali position is the decisive constraint. The record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the reason as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” It also states the moratorium rule directly: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is simple: although KBLI 10798 is nationally foreign-open up to 100%, a foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the record’s Bali-side rule. The difference is not a Bali ownership percentage or a separate local cap; it is a registration block tied to the Bali moratorium and the risk class described in the record.
